scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.voiceover: Is oxytocin really the love hormone?

scenes.visual: Two figures slide together, a warm teal pulse blooms between them — the bonding effect of oxytocin.
scenes.voiceover: Oxytocin is the bonding chemical. A hug, a shared laugh — and it glues you to your people.

scenes.visual: Teal in-group dots cluster inside a navy ring; a coral outsider dot gets nudged further away as the ring holds firm.
scenes.voiceover: But the same glue draws a line. As it pulls your group closer, it pushes outsiders further away.

scenes.visual: The navy ring springs outward; the coral outsider dot enters the circle and turns teal; a mustard warm pulse blooms at the center.
scenes.voiceover: The fix isn't less bonding — it's a bigger circle. Find one thing you share, and 'them' becomes 'us'.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it a two-bar chart springs up: tall teal YOUR GROUP bar vs short navy OUTSIDERS bar under a TRUST headline.
scenes.cardText: Oxytocin boosts in-group trust — not trust in general.
scenes.voiceover: Oxytocin drives in-group favoritism: it raises trust and cooperation inside your group, but not toward outsiders.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the widening circle animation plays with the outsider dot turning teal. Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
Feeling 'us vs them'?
Name one thing you share with 'them'.
scenes.voiceover: Next time you feel 'us versus them,' name one thing you share with them.
